Golf.title: At Open Championship, golf's stars face unique opponent for final time
Golf.summary: The Open Championship is a celebration. As the year's final major, it's also now the final time golf's stars face a unique opponent. The post At Open Championship, golf’s stars face unique opponent for final time appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
The Open Championship is a celebration — of golf’s beginnings, its past champions, its DNA, its homelands. For the last seven years, since the PGA Championship moved to May, it has also served as the final chapter of golf’s major season — the last chance for players to etch their names into history before the eight-and-a-half-month wait for the Masters begins.

It’s also the final time of the year that the faces of golf, the players around whom the sport revolves, face a unique opponent: grand, existential, possibly unanswerable questions about dreams, legacy, the long arc of pro golf, mortality and everything in between.

Golf.title: This Open Championship has some competition: England's World Cup charge
Golf.summary: English sports fans’ cups runneth over this week, and we’re not talking only about the Open Championship at Royal Birkdale. The post This Open Championship has some competition: England’s World Cup charge appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
The good people in the coastal northwest England suburb of Southport are mad about golf, just as they are about four-or-so hours north in the Land of the Scots, just as they are a short paddle across the Irish Sea in Northern Ireland, which seven years ago, with the Royal & Ancient’s blessing, reinitiated its standing as Open Championship host territory.

This week’s Open at Royal Birkdale (est. 1889) was such a hot ticket that the R&A sold more than 300,000 of them, from an applicant pool of 1 million. “A record attendance,” R&A chief Mark Darbon woofed Wednesday at Birkdale. (And just wait until next year, at the mother of all Open venues, the Old Course at St. Andrews. The R&A opened the ticket ballot for that event nine days ago and already has received 750,000 requests.)

Golf.title: Data analysis: How each LIV Golf player could win The Open
Golf.summary: Data analysis: How each LIV Golf player could win The Open LIV Golf
Golf.body:
Go inside the stats to see which of the 15 LIV Golf players in this week’s Open Championship field have the best chance of claiming the Claret Jug at Royal Birkdale. Driving Accuracy: Royal Birkdale is an intriguing driving golf course. It doesn’t reward the longest driver, it doesn’t reward the straightest driver, it rewards the player who can pick there best lines and controls the ball the best for four days. Birkdale will make players and caddies make decisions to use less than driver, lay back of the traps, accept longer approaches and avoid running out into rough. Position is more important than inaccurate length.

150-200 yard approaches: The strategy off the tee here will result in longer approach shots. There are two par 3 holes over 220 yards, three par 4 holes over 500 yards as well as five that are over 450 yards. The 150-200 yard range will be key this week and whoever can execute well from here will be teeing off late on Sunday.

Golf.title: How to shoot lower scores without swinging your best
Golf.summary: GOLF Teacher to Watch Chad Gibbs explains how you can shoot low scores without necessarily having your best swing. The post How to shoot lower scores without swinging your best appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Most golfers believe they should shoot their handicap — or better — every time they tee it up. Part of golf’s magic is the belief that today could be the day you shoot a personal best. Even when someone tells you to temper your expectations, it rarely quiets the desire to play your absolute best.

One of the most common frustrations golfers express is that they can’t take their range game to the course. They flush shots during practice, only to struggle once the scorecard comes out. But expecting your range game to translate directly to the course, or believing you should beat your handicap every round, is a flawed way of thinking. Looking at your game through a different lens can help you become a more consistent scorer.

Golf.title: British Open: With LIV Golf standing on its last leg, it needs Jon Rahm or Bryson DeChambeau to show up at Royal Birkdale
Golf.summary: British Open: With LIV Golf standing on its last leg, it needs Jon Rahm or Bryson DeChambeau to show up at Royal Birkdale AOL.co.uk
Golf.body:
LIV Golf is not in a good place entering the final major championship of the season. Now more than ever, with the Saudi Arabian-backed venture seemingly standing on its last leg, it desperately needs Jon Rahm or Bryson DeChambeau to show out at Royal Birkdale. If they don't, it could speed up the league's already pending demise.

And based on how things have gone for LIV Golf's biggest names in the major championships lately, that actually might be a big ask. Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund announced earlier this year that it was pulling funding from LIV Golf after the 2026 season. The PIF backed the league initially and helped it off the ground, and has reportedly invested more than $5 billion into it since 2022. But the venture has struggled to gain real traction, and has even lost multiple notable golfers back to the PGA Tour, so the PIF opted to back out altogether.

As legalized sports gambling rises in popularity in the U.S., and its negative impacts ripple through grandstands across the country, golf has not been left untouched. While players in other sports have been caught betting on and influencing games, the fans are the problem in golf.

The former U.S. Open champ laid out two distinct ways sports gambling is becoming a “problem” in golf: fan abuse toward players and hecklers trying to influence play.

Golf.title: Decision on changing Open final round timings to follow England World Cup semi-final
Golf.summary: Any change to The Open's final round timings, to avoid a clash with the World Cup final should England get there, will be made in "the next 48 hours" and be "subtle" says R&A chief Mark Darbon.
Golf.body:
A decision on whether to move the final round of The Open to avoid a clash with the World Cup final will be made after England's semi-final against Argentina on Wednesday. If England beat Argentina - which kicks off at 20:00 BST and will be shown live across the BBC - they will reach Sunday's World Cup final for the first time since winning it in 1966.

Sunday's play at Royal Birkdale is scheduled to finish around 90 minutes before football's showpiece match kicks off in New Jersey at 20:00, with Spain already in the final. Should the golf go to a play-off, the two events are at risk of overlapping, creating a quandary for fans and broadcasters.

Golf.title: Why Royal Birkdale could mark the beginning of the end for LIV Golf amid $433m cash crisis
Golf.summary: Why Royal Birkdale could mark the beginning of the end for LIV Golf amid $433m cash crisis dailyclubgolf.com
Golf.body:
The Open Championship tees off at Royal Birkdale this week with the world's best players in the field, but it could also be the last major where LIV Golf still exists as a functioning league.

LIV Golf CEO Scott O'Neil is racing to raise between US$250 million and US$300 million, equivalent to $361 million to $433 million Australian, by September 1, according to Fox Sports on July 15. Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund announced in April it will not fund LIV beyond this season. Bloomberg reported in May that LIV has begun laying the groundwork to potentially file for bankruptcy in the United States at season's end.

Golf.title: Confident MacIntyre eyes Open Championship glory
Golf.summary: Scotland's number one Robert MacIntyre believes he is a much improved golfer from the one who teed up at his first Open Championship at Royal Portrush in 2019.
Golf.body:
Scotland's number one Robert MacIntyre believes he is a much improved golfer from the one who teed up at his first Open Championship at Royal Portrush in 2019. That was MacIntyre's debut appearance at a major and he finished sixth behind home favourite Shane Lowry.

Since then, the 29-year-old has become a top 20 player in the world rankings and heads into this week's tournament after finishing third at the Scottish Open. "In 2019, I felt like I was just being part of the tournament," MacIntyre said. "I was making up the numbers. I was just seeing how well I could do in this event.

Baked fairways, stiff breezes, iconic clubhouses and the smell of the sea. Along with unmistakable yellow scoreboards and massive crowds, all are memories of Open Championships past — links golf’s greatest test, staged at world-class venues.

That would be an ambitious itinerary, but for a group that can spare a week, the northwest coast of England will more than deliver.

Golf.title: What is the prize money at The Open 2026?

Golf.body:
The winner of the 2026 Open Championship at Royal Birkdale will receive a total prize of $3.2m (£2.4m). The total prize pool of $17.75m (£13.3m) is an increase of $750,000 (£560,000) from the 2025 tournament at Royal Portrush, while the winner's prize has increased by $100,000 (£74,600).

All players who finish in the top three will receive over $1.1m (£820,000) each, while a top-seven finish guarantees a prize north of $500,000 (£372,900) each. Prize money at The Open will only be awarded to professional players.

Badminton.title: China Open: Rescued by Resolve
Badminton.summary: China Open: Rescued by Resolve BWF World Tour
Badminton.body:
Three match points down and staring at another early exit, Weng Hong Yang found something that had been missing for much of 2026 – belief. The 2024 champion produced the comeback of the opening day, saving three match points at 20-17 before completing a thrilling 15-21 21-17 22-20 victory over men’s singles third seed Anders Antonsen in 84 unforgettable minutes at VICTOR China Open 2026.

It was a finish few inside the Olympic Sports Center Gymnasium saw coming. Weng had spent most of the afternoon chasing the Dane. After falling 11-6 behind in the opening game, he fought back to level at 14-all before Antonsen regained control. The Chinese player responded with a steadier display in the second game to force a decider but the momentum swung back heavily in Antonsen’s favour as he raced to a commanding 12-4 lead.

Badminton.title: 'Importance of finding...': Virat Kohli’s one piece of advice helped PV Sindhu end her longest title drought and win a BWF Super 750 title in Japan Open
Badminton.summary: 'Importance of finding...': Virat Kohli’s one piece of advice helped PV Sindhu end her longest title drought and win a BWF Super 750 title in Japan Open The Economic Times
Badminton.body:
The 31-year-old shuttler won her maiden BWF Super 750 title at the Japan Open after defeating three-time world champion Akane Yamaguchi of Japan in straight games in the women's singles final in Tokyo on Sunday. The triumph marked Sindhu's biggest title since her historic BWF World Championships victory in 2019. Before this, her recent titles included the 2022 Singapore Open Super 500 and the 2024 Syed Modi International Super 300.

With the Japan Open win, Sindhu became the first Indian shuttler to claim the prestigious title and ended a title drought of more than two years. Sindhu's journey to the Japan Open crown was far from easy. The previous two years were among the toughest periods of her career. A stress fracture interrupted her progress, while her Paris Olympics campaign ended with an early exit.Repeated injuries and rehabilitation challenges made her comeback difficult. With every setback, the pressure surrounding one of India's most celebrated athletes continued to grow. However, Sindhu found a new perspective during a conversation with Virat Kohli, who himself has experienced the pressure of performing at the highest level.

Badminton.title: Japan Open: Another Peak for Popov
Badminton.summary: Japan Open: Another Peak for Popov BWF World Tour
Badminton.body:
Christo Popov delivered a near-flawless performance to claim the DAIHATSU Japan Open 2026 to earn a morale-boosting title win ahead of the BWF World Championships next month. Koki Watanabe had had a draining three-game match against Yushi Tanaka in the semifinals, but to his credit, the home hope didn’t make it easy for the Frenchman, particularly in the second game. Watanabe had his chances in the second, but Popov’s greater sharpness and ability to last the rallies helped him nudge the tape, 21-11 21-19, for his third title of the year.

“This means a lot… it’s confirmation of what I was talking about for the last few months or weeks,” said Popov. “For me, it’s a very big achievement. Most of all, I like to play in Japan. I’m very happy to bring the title this year.

Badminton.title: PV Sindhu scripts history with Japan Open win, eyes BWF World Championships
Badminton.summary: PV Sindhu scripts history with Japan Open win, eyes BWF World Championships connectedtoindia.com
Badminton.body:
Two-time Olympics medallist PV Sindhu on Sunday, July 19, said that while she never stopped believing in herself, her victory at the Japan Open Super 750 reaffirmed that it is not over yet. The shuttler said she is now eyeing the upcoming BWF World Championships, scheduled to take place in New Delhi from August 17 to 23.

Sindhu’s win in straight games (21-17, 21-17) over Japan’s Akane Yamaguchi helped her clinch a first major title in two years, and she also became the first-ever Indian to win the tournament.

Badminton.title: PV Sindhu scripts history, becomes first Indian to win BWF Japan Open
Badminton.summary: PV Sindhu scripts history, becomes first Indian to win BWF Japan Open WION
Badminton.body:
Two-time Olympic medallist PV Sindhu delivered a throwback performance, defeating Akane Yamaguchi in straight games and capturing her maiden Super 750 title at the Japan Open on Sunday. She became the first Indian to win the tournament, sealing a 21-17, 21-17 victory over the three-time world champion and ending a title drought of more than two years. It also marked her biggest triumph since the World Championships crown in 2019, with her previous title coming at the Syed Modi International in 2024.

Yamaguchi, playing her sixth Japan Open final, had enjoyed the upper hand in recent meetings, Sindhu had not beaten her in a completed match in four years, with their last full-match win dating back to the Thailand Open in 2022. Their earlier clash at the Malaysia Open this year ended prematurely after Yamaguchi retired following the opening game.

Badminton.title: Japan Open: Kong Makes Triumphant Return After Surgery
Badminton.summary: Japan Open: Kong Makes Triumphant Return After Surgery BWF World Tour
Badminton.body:
Kong Hee Yong’s return to competitive badminton following a right knee surgery culminated in a dream title, with the women’s doubles final among the most dramatic in recent times.

Kong was out of action after the Badminton Asia Team Championships in February for the knee surgery and rehab; the world No.8 making a return with Kim Hye Jeong only at the DAIHATSU Japan Open 2026. The high point of the return was in the final game against Jia Yi Fan/Zhang Shu Xian, which went the Koreans’ way, 14-21 21-15 30-29. The see-sawing final game saw either side have six match points before Zhang Shu Xian blew a kill just wide, and the Koreans collapsing in a flood of emotions.

Badminton.title: Japan Open: Pusarla Breaks Title Drought
Badminton.summary: Japan Open: Pusarla Breaks Title Drought BWF World Tour
Badminton.body:
It has been four years since Pusarla V Sindhu won a title at the upper end of the HSBC BWF World Tour. Her last Super 500 title was over four years ago — the Singapore Open in May 2022. And while there were Super 300 titles and the Commonwealth Games gold in 2022, her last major title had come seven years ago, at the BWF World Championships 2019.

The relief and joy at breaking this pattern was written all over her face as she revelled in the feeling of winning the DAIHATSU Japan Open 2026; the Super 750 triumph marking a high point in her career, and putting her back in the conversation as a contender at the upcoming BWF World Championships.

Badminton.title: BWF World Championships 2026 Countdown Begins with Mascot Peacko and Official Anthem Launch
Badminton.summary: BWF World Championships 2026 Countdown Begins with Mascot Peacko and Official Anthem Launch Daily Pioneer
Badminton.body:
Sports is not simply about winning medals; it is about nurturing talent, building a vibrant sporting culture and strengthening the ecosystem that enables athletes to thrive. Echoing this vision, the countdown to the BWF World Championships 2026 officially commenced with the unveiling of the tournament’s official mascot and official anthem on Saturday, July 18, 2026 at New Delhi.

The championship, scheduled to be held at the Indira Gandhi Indoor Stadium from August 17 to 23, 2026, will bring together the world’s finest shuttlers and mark the first time India will host badminton’s premier event.

Badminton.title: Hybrid shuttles, bird nets as BWF World Championships plug India Open glitches
Badminton.summary: Hybrid shuttles, bird nets as BWF World Championships plug India Open glitches The Times of India
Badminton.body:
BWF World Championships to kick-off, organisers on Saturday promised a trouble-free tournament after last year's India Open was marred by pigeon droppings, a monkey intrusion, dust and facility concerns. TOI has learnt that cost-effective hybrid shuttlecocks will also be used, amid soaring feather shuttle prices.

Badminton Association of India (BAI) general secretary Sanjay Mishra said the shortcomings exposed during the India Open have been comprehensively addressed ahead of the Aug 17-23 event, which is expected to cost the federation anywhere between Rs 15-20 crore to host.

Badminton.title: BWF World Championships: Sports Minister Mandaviya unveils mascot ‘Peacko’, official anthem ahead of home event
Badminton.summary: BWF World Championships: Sports Minister Mandaviya unveils mascot ‘Peacko’, official anthem ahead of home event The Statesman
Badminton.body:
Pullela Gopichand hailed India hosting the BWF World Championships after 17 years and backed PV Sindhu to continue her resurgence ahead of the Japan Open final. With just 30 days remaining until the BWF World Championships return to India after 17 years, Union Sports Minister Dr. Mansukh Mandaviya on Saturday unveiled the official mascot, Peacko, and launched the tournament’s official anthem, marking the beginning of the final countdown to badminton’s flagship event.

The launch ceremony, held in New Delhi, was attended by Badminton Association of India (BAI) President and Assam Chief Minister Dr. Himanta Biswa Sarma, BAI General Secretary Sanjay Mishra, Indian badminton chief national coach Pullela Gopichand, Sports Authority of India Director General Hari Ranjan Rao and members of the badminton fraternity.

Badminton.title: Japan Open: Pusarla Back in Title Contention
Badminton.summary: Japan Open: Pusarla Back in Title Contention BWF World Tour
Badminton.body:
It has been a while since Pusarla V Sindhu made a major final. Her last World Tour final at a Super 500 tournament was over 25 months ago – the Malaysia Masters in May 2024. For anything above that level, the clock has to be dialled back 55 months, when she was in the title round of the HSBC BWF World Tour Finals 2021.

The return to title contention came with her first victory over Chen Yu Fei in six matches. Chen retired with a pulled muscle in her right thigh, with the Indian leading 21-19 15-10, but the retirement took nothing away from Pusarla, who looked close to her best all match and had Chen fighting a rearguard battle throughout.

Badminton.title: Insider Purchases Worth AU$1.17m See Losses As BlackWall Market Value Drops To AU$21m
Badminton.summary: Insider Purchases Worth AU$1.17m See Losses As BlackWall Market Value Drops To AU$21m simplywall.st
Badminton.body:
The recent price decline of 12% in BlackWall Limited's (ASX:BWF) stock may have disappointed insiders who bought AU$1.17m worth of shares at an average price of AU$0.20 in the past 12 months. Insiders purchase with the hope of seeing their investments increase in value over time. However, due to recent losses, their initial investment is now only worth AU$725.9k, which is not great.

While we would never suggest that investors should base their decisions solely on what the directors of a company have been doing, logic dictates you should pay some attention to whether insiders are buying or selling shares.

Badminton.title: Japan Open: Yamaguchi Leads Home Surge
Badminton.summary: Japan Open: Yamaguchi Leads Home Surge BWF World Tour
Badminton.body:
Once Akane Yamaguchi had staged a surreal comeback, there was no looking back for Japan. The home fans’ reigning deity, nearly down and out against Kim Ga Eun, broke her opponent’s heart as she completed her 11th straight victory over the Korean.

What followed was a dream day for Japan, with Yushi Tanaka upstaging No.2 seed Kunlavut Vitidsarn to enter his maiden Super 750 semifinal, Koki Watanabe taking down third seed Anders Antonsen, and Kodai Naraoka prevailing in a 98-minute marathon against Alwi Farhan.

Badminton.title: Rising star Dalvi reaches BWF Italian International quarter-finals
Badminton.summary: Rising star Dalvi reaches BWF Italian International quarter-finals Luton Today
Badminton.body:
Luton badminton star Nadeem Dalvi has taken another significant step towards his dream of representing England on the biggest stages after an outstanding performance at the BWF Italian International in Bolzano recently.

The 21-year-old battled his way from the qualifying rounds to reach the quarter-finals of the prestigious international tournament, producing a string of impressive victories against experienced opponents from around the globe. His run of successes included triumphs over India’s Koushik Dinesh Mudlukoplu and Suveer Pradhan before defeating Shashwat Dalal in straight games, underlining his ability to compete with players from one of badminton’s strongest nations.

Badminton.title: BWF World Championships 2026: Chirag Shetty says focus is on World Championships and Asian Games
Badminton.summary: BWF World Championships 2026: Chirag Shetty says focus is on World Championships and Asian Games Telangana Today
Badminton.body:
India's men's doubles star Chirag Shetty says he and partner Satwiksairaj Rankireddy are focused on peaking for the BWF World Championships and the Asian Games. The duo will also look to defend their historic men's doubles gold at the 2026 Asian Games.

New Delhi: India’s star doubles shuttler Chirag Shetty says he and long-time partner Satwiksairaj Rankireddy are fully focused on making the most of two of the biggest events on the badminton calendar this year, the BWF World Championships and the Asian Games.

Badminton.title: Japan Open: Malaysians Spring Surprise
Badminton.summary: Japan Open: Malaysians Spring Surprise BWF World Tour
Badminton.body:
Just five tournaments into their partnership, Jimmy Wong and Cheng Su Yin knocked out in-form pair Mathias Christiansen and Alexandra Boje on their way to a first semifinal. It was Christiansen and Boje’s earliest defeat since the All England in March, after which they had embarked on a brilliant run which saw them win four titles from five finals.

Wong and Cheng, whose partnership started at the Malaysia Masters where they ran into the Danes, turned it around today with a calm performance, disallowing the Danes any substantial opening.

Badminton.title: Lakshya Sen leads India's hopes as Shi Yu Qi, Kunlavut & Popov among top international stars to light up
Badminton.summary: Lakshya Sen leads India's hopes as Shi Yu Qi, Kunlavut & Popov among top international stars to light up The Times of India
Badminton.body:
BWF World Championships returns to India after 17 years, the spotlight will firmly be on a star-studded men's singles field. Scheduled from Aug 17–23 at the Indira Gandhi (IG) indoor stadium here, the tournament will feature some of badminton's biggest names alongside the sport's next generation of stars. Here are five players who have all the ingredients to leave their mark on the championships. TOI takes a look...

The reigning world champion and current World No. 1, Shi Yu Qi heads to New Delhi as one of the biggest favourites for the title. Widely regarded as one of the most complete players on the circuit, the Chinese star is known for his deceptive stroke play, tactical intelligence and ability to dictate rallies. After finishing runner-up at the 2018 World Championships, Shi completed his redemption story by winning his maiden world title in 2025. With multiple Super 1000 titles and Thomas Cup triumphs to his name, the 30-year-old will be eager to defend his crown on Indian soil.

Badminton.title: Japan Open: Sensational Day for USA
Badminton.summary: Japan Open: Sensational Day for USA BWF World Tour
Badminton.body:
At the end of a day in which Lauren Lam/Allison Lee had pulled off the sensational upset of third seeds Baek Na Na/Lee So Hee, there was more good news for USA at the DAIHATSU Japan Open 2026.

Chen Zhi Yi and Presley Smith followed up in the last match with an upset of their own, knocking out world No.16 Daniel Lundgaard/Mads Vestergaard in straight games. For Team USA, it couldn’t have been scripted better, with both pairs making the quarterfinals of an HSBC BWF World Tour Super 750 event for the first time.

Badminton.title: Five men’s singles players to watch at BWF World Championships India 2026
Badminton.summary: Five men’s singles players to watch at BWF World Championships India 2026 The News Mill
Badminton.body:
The BWF World Championships will return to India for the first time in 17 years, with the men’s singles competition expected to feature some of the sport’s biggest stars alongside emerging talent. The tournament will take place from August 17 to 23 at the Indira Gandhi Indoor Stadium in New Delhi, bringing the world’s top badminton players to India for one of the sport’s premier events.

The men’s singles draw promises to be a major attraction, showcasing established champions and rising stars. Here are five players expected to make a significant impact at the championships.

Badminton.title: Japan Open: Sensational Day for USA as Lam/Lee Author Upset
Badminton.summary: Japan Open: Sensational Day for USA as Lam/Lee Author Upset BWF World Tour
Badminton.body:
Lauren Lam and Allison Lee delivered the biggest result of their nascent career to achieve their first HSBC BWF World Tour Super 750 quarterfinals at the DAIHATSU Japan Open 2026.

The USA pair were a game and 1-9 down to world No.3 Baek Ha Na/Lee So Hee before staging the turnaround. Chipping away at the deficit and pulling level at 12, the underdogs gained in confidence with each point and had the Koreans under pressure.

Badminton.title: Japan Open: Vitidsarn Passes Stiff Opening Test
Badminton.summary: Japan Open: Vitidsarn Passes Stiff Opening Test BWF World Tour
Badminton.body:
Returning to the circuit after a back muscle tear disrupted his last two tournaments, Kunlavut Vitidsarn survived a stiff opening test from Ayush Shetty at the DAIHATSU Japan Open 2026.

The No.2 seed had retired from his last two matches, at the Singapore Open and Indonesia Open, and said he was feeling much better, although he had yet to fully recover. Against Shetty, who had beaten him during their last contest at the Badminton Asia Championships in April. Vitidsarn took his time to find the answers, before he eventually pulled away in the third game.
